newsitem.title: USA: Pakistan to import more wheat in 97/98-US attache.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan to import more wheat in 97/98-US attache.

text.p: Pakistan will be a market for three million tonnes of imported wheat to offset a likely downturn in domestic production, the U.S. attache in Islamabad said in a report released Friday.

The attache forecast imports of 2.4 million tonnes this marketing year. Of that, 1.8 million tonnes would come from the United States. U.S. sales in 1997/98 could be 2.5 million tonnes, the attache wrote.
"Availability of a large required GSM-102 program will be critical in determining U.S. market share in MY1997/98," the report said.
"Early season dry weather in rainfed areas and declining fertilizer use are reported reasons for the poor harvest forecast of 15.8 MMT for MY1997/98 wheat crop," the attache wrote.
Pakistan's rice crop was forecast at 16.9 million tonnes for 1996/97.
Pakistan exported 1.64 million tonnes of rice in 1995/96. Exports during 1996/97 are estimated at 1.7 MMT.
